snip.t: Nephritic entities: PSGN in children is self‑limited with >90 % full recovery; RPGN carries a high risk of ESRD unless rapid immunosuppression and plasma exchange are instituted.

Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 ml/min) or rapidly rising creatinine: Initiate urgent plasma exchange (if ANCA‑associated) and start high‑dose intravenous glucocorticoid pulse — Removes pathogenic antibodies and controls inflammation while definitive therapy is arranged
RPGN and lupus nephritis: an emergency: high-dose steroids, cyclophosphamide, plasma exchange for anti-GBM, and renal support.
ADAMTS13 activity (if TMA suspected): Distinguish TTP — Severely reduced activity supports TTP; requires plasma exchange.

Definitive therapy directed at the identified mechanism (immunosuppression for AIHA, avoidance of oxidants for G6PD, antimalarials for malaria, splenectomy for hereditary spherocytosis when indicated, plasma exchange for TTP).
Guillain‑Barré syndrome: IV immunoglobulin or plasma exchange — Modulates immune attack on peripheral nerves
Severity guides urgency of immunotherapy (IVIG or plasma exchange for moderate‑severe GBS) and need for intensive monitoring (respiratory function, cardiac rhythm).
Same as above: Plasma exchange (PE) – 4‑5 exchanges over 1‑2 weeks — Ensure central line patency, replace electrolytes
